passages.heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Governor
passages.text: Scott Jewett is a leader, entrepreneur, innovator, lifelong problem solver, and family man who calls Boca Raton home. Like so many Floridians, he and his wife Regina face the daily realities of homeownership, rising insurance costs , and the desire to leave a freer, more prosperous state to the next generation.

passages.heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Governor
passages.text: He is running for Governor because he believes Florida can do better , with less government overreach, more individual liberty, and practical solutions that put people first.

passages.heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Governor
passages.text: His agenda centers on a robust economy with more living wage jobs , real educational choice, public safety, lower taxes, and a government that respects the rights of every Floridian, regardless of which major party they usually vote for.

passages.heading: Fighting for Families in Florida
passages.text: Floridians are feeling the squeeze every month . Insurance premiums keep climbing, everyday costs keep rising, and too much of your hard earned money disappears into government waste. Scott Jewett is fighting to fix the insurance affordability crisis, cut taxes, shrink the size of government, and put real solutions in place that help families keep more of what they earn. He believes Florida can do better when we put people first .

passages.heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Lieutenant Governor
passages.text: Nicole Skelly lives in Milton, Florida with her husband and their two children. Together they have owned and run a construction business for many years.

passages.heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Lieutenant Governor
passages.text: As a small business owner and mom, Nicole knows the daily pressure of rising costs, heavy rules, and government overreach . She believes parents and hardworking families should be trusted more than bureaucrats.

passages.heading: Libertarian Candidate for Florida Lieutenant Governor
passages.text: Nicole is ready to help cut the red tape that drives up prices, protect parental rights , and fight for a Florida where people can keep more of what they earn and live free. She wants her kids, and every Florida family, to have the same chance that hard work should still provide.

passages.heading: Volunteer
passages.text: Join the team that’s fighting for liberty in Florida. Help us knock doors, make calls, and spread the message that real change is possible. Every hour counts.

passages.heading: Stay Informed
passages.text: Get campaign updates, event invites, and policy news delivered straight to your inbox. Stay connected and never miss a chance to make your voice heard.

passages.heading: Register to Vote
passages.text: Your vote is your power. Confirm you’re registered and ready to support liberty at the ballot box. Florida’s future depends on it.

passages.heading: Major Donors
passages.text: Ready to make a major impact? Join the supporters fueling a serious challenge to the status quo and help put liberty back on the ballot.

passages.heading: Answers to common questions.
passages.text: Here you’ll find clear, straightforward answers to the questions we hear most often from Floridians. If you don’t see your question listed, feel free to reach out; we’re happy to communicate with everyone, you voices matter.

passages.heading: Answers to common questions.
passages.text: Check out the frequently asked questions page for more questions and answers.

passages.heading: How will you actually lower my homeowners insurance premiums?
passages.text: Government rules and state programs keep pushing your insurance higher. We will cut those rules and open the market so more companies compete for your business. More competition means lower premiums for Florida homeowners.

passages.heading: How are you different from the other candidates?
passages.text: We're not part of the two big parties that keep raising costs and taking more control. I trust parents, workers, and small business owners more than government. Most Floridians already live this way; they just want to be left alone. That’s the real difference.

passages.heading: What’s your plan to reduce the overall cost of living in Florida; groceries, housing, insurance, and utilities?
passages.text: Cut the rules and taxes that drive prices up. Open markets so more companies compete on groceries, housing, insurance, and power. When government gets out of the way, costs fall for working Florida families.

passages.heading: What’s your position on school choice and making sure parents have real options for their kids’ education?
passages.text: Parents should decide where their kids go to school. We support real school choice so education dollars follow the child, not the system. Public, private, charter, or homeschool, families pick what works best. Bureaucrats don’t.

passages.heading: News
passages.text: Read the latest campaign news, press releases, and media coverage as Scott and Nicole take the message of liberty across Florida.

passages.heading: Videos
passages.text: Watch speeches, interviews, and campaign videos. Hear directly from Scott and Nicole on the issues that matter most to Floridians.

passages.heading: Social Media
passages.text: Follow the campaign for real-time updates, live events, and conversations. Join the growing movement for liberty in Florida.

passages.heading: Join the Fight for an Affordable Florida
passages.text: Be part of the grassroots movement that is representing all Floridians!

passages.heading: Your information. Our Policies.
passages.text: This is a grassroots campaign website, not a store and not a government portal. If you write us, donate, volunteer, or ask for updates, we will treat that information like it belongs to you, and we will only use it to run this campaign and to follow Florida law.

passages.heading: Who we are
passages.text: Scott Jewett is the Libertarian candidate for Governor of Florida. Nicole Skelly is the Libertarian candidate for Lieutenant Governor. We trust people more than government. That includes how we handle the information you choose to give us.

passages.heading: Who we are
passages.text: Questions about this policy: use the Contact page at scottjewett.com or email the campaign at [INSERT CAMPAIGN EMAIL]. Do not publish this page until that address is real.

passages.heading: How we use it
passages.text: Comply with law, respond to lawful requests, and protect the campaign, donors, volunteers, and the public.

passages.heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
passages.text: This is a campaign for Governor and Lieutenant Governor of Florida. It is a state race. Donor reporting is governed by Chapter 106, Florida Statutes, and the Florida Division of Elections — not by a generic “business privacy” template.

passages.heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
passages.text: Candidates must report contributions. Reports include the full name and address of each contributor. For contributions over $100, occupation is also reported. Those reports are public. If you donate above that threshold, your name, address, occupation, and amount can appear in public filings.

passages.heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
passages.text: That is the tradeoff the law makes so people can see who funds campaigns. We will not pretend otherwise.

passages.heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
passages.text: Cash contributions are limited by Florida law. Do not mail cash to the website. Use the official donate form or the instructions the campaign publishes.

passages.heading: Florida campaign-finance reporting
passages.text: Builder: link Florida Division of Elections campaign finance search if you want a public-records sentence. Optional:

passages.text: We do not sell, rent, or lease your personal information to companies that want to pitch you a product.

passages.heading: Who we share it with
passages.text: Service vendors who run the site, process donations, send email, host forms, or provide analytics. They get only what they need to do that job. The Florida Division of Elections and other government offices when the law requires a report or a response.

passages.heading: Who we share it with

passages.heading: Email, updates, and texts
passages.text: We will not sell your text opt-in, consent, or related mobile information to third parties. Vendors who actually send the texts are not a “sale.” Florida law has separate rules for political telephone and text ads, including “Paid for by” language on certain messages. We will follow those rules.

passages.text: Remember a preference, such as a cookie banner choice.

passages.heading: Cookies and analytics
passages.text: You can block non-essential cookies in your browser. The site may work less smoothly if you do. We do not use your visit to this site to build a commercial advertising profile to sell to other businesses.

passages.heading: Cookies and analytics
passages.text: If we use a tool such as Google Analytics, it is to understand whether the site is doing its job — not to run a retail storefront.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: Read the site without submitting a form.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: Give us only the fields a form requires.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: Ask us to correct a name, email, or address we use to contact you.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: Ask what campaign-contact information we have on you, subject to the records we must keep under Florida law.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: We may not delete a donation record, occupation field, or other data that campaign-finance law requires us to keep and report. We can stop using your email for updates.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: To make a request, use the Contact page or email [INSERT CAMPAIGN EMAIL] with “Privacy request” in the subject line. We will verify that the request is really from you before changing a record.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: Some states have consumer privacy statutes written for businesses that sell data. This committee is a political campaign. We do not sell personal information for money. We do not use this website as a commercial store.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: If a law still gives you a right we can honor without breaking Florida campaign-finance rules, write us and we will handle it in good faith. Campaign-finance reports already filed cannot be unpublished by a website form.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: We use reasonable safeguards — encrypted connections on the site, limited staff access, and vendors who are supposed to protect payment data. No website is perfectly safe. Do not send Social Security numbers, passwords, or extra financial details by ordinary email.

passages.heading: Your choices
passages.text: We keep information as long as the campaign needs it to communicate, comply with law, handle disputes, and close out the committee. Florida record-retention rules for campaign reports apply even after Election Day.

passages.heading: Children
passages.text: This site is for adults who can vote, donate, and volunteer. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If a parent believes a child submitted a form, write us and we will delete what the law allows us to delete.

passages.heading: Children
passages.text: The site may link to donation processors, social networks, the Libertarian Party of Florida, news stories, or government pages. Those sites have their own rules. Read theirs before you submit information there.

passages.heading: Florida families are paying more and getting less
passages.text: Florida does not have one money problem. It has a stack of them . Insurance. Taxes. Housing. Power bills. Healthcare. Government growth. They all land on the same kitchen table.

passages.heading: Florida families are paying more and getting less
passages.text: Scott Jewett and Nicole Skelly trust you. You know how to raise your kids, run your shop, and take care of your family. You should keep more of what you earn . You should live free.

passages.heading: Florida families are paying more and getting less
passages.text: Scroll down to get more information about where we stand on the issues and what we plan to do. You can also click on one of the issues from the list to go directly to that issue .

passages.heading: Florida families are paying more and getting less
passages.text: Scroll Down or Select an Issue From the List!

passages.heading: Florida families are paying more and getting less

passages.heading: Stop the Squeeze on Florida Families
passages.text: We have an affordability crisis. Groceries, housing, homeowners insurance, property taxes, utilities, gas, car insurance, car payments, health insurance, childcare, and eating out are more expensive now. Utilities keep climbing. Parents pick up extra hours. Gig workers drive later. Small shops stay open longer and still fall behind.

passages.heading: Stop the Squeeze on Florida Families
passages.text: Government did not feel that squeeze first. Families did. When Tallahassee or Washington adds a rule, a fee, or a new program, the cost shows up in the price of milk, the rent check, and the mortgage payment on a modest home.

passages.heading: Stop the Squeeze on Florida Families
passages.text: Floridians are not asking for a lecture about the economy. They are asking why they work harder and keep less.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Hardworking people should keep more of what they earn. Government should get out of the way so prices can come down and paychecks can stretch further.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Cost of living is not one bill. It is insurance, property taxes, housing, energy, healthcare, and red tape stacked on the same family. Fix those pressures and everyday life gets cheaper.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: We trust Floridians to run their own budgets . Government should have to live on one too.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Treat cost of living as the test for every state decision: does this make life cheaper for families, or more expensive?

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Cut rules and fees that raise the price of food, housing, energy, insurance, and hiring.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Stop shifting government costs onto household bills.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Force agencies to show how new rules hit parents, retirees, renters, and small shops before those rules take effect.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Tie the rest of this agenda together — insurance, taxes, housing, healthcare, energy, and spending — so the kitchen table squeeze actually eases.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Florida families should not have to work two jobs to afford one life. Keep what you earn. Live free.

passages.heading: Fix the Insurance Affordability Crisis
passages.text: Florida homeowners pay some of the highest premiums in the country . When the roof leaks or the storm hits, too little of that money comes back to fix the house.

passages.heading: Fix the Insurance Affordability Crisis
passages.text: Retirees on fixed incomes open a renewal letter and wonder if they can stay. Young families trying to buy a first home get priced out before they ever unpack. Small landlords raise rent because the premium jumped again. Coastal towns watch private insurers leave, then watch Citizens grow.

passages.heading: Fix the Insurance Affordability Crisis
passages.text: The system is broken by waste, lawsuits that do not help homeowners, rules that chase companies out, and claims practices that grind families down. Storm risk is real. The bloated system on top of that risk is a choice.

passages.heading: Fix the Insurance Affordability Crisis
passages.text: Floridians are not asking for another press conference. They are asking why they pay six times more in premiums than they ever see paid out in claims.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Insurance should protect the home, not feed a bloated system . Premiums should be honest. Claims should get paid. Families should not be trapped with one expensive option.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Homeowners deserve competition, clear rules, and a market that wants to write coverage in Florida . Citizens should be a safety net, not the default company for half the state.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Scott has already drafted insurance reform work because he refuses to accept that this is “just Florida.” People who pay the bill deserve a system that works when they need it.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Cut the waste that drives premiums up and keeps claim dollars from reaching damaged homes.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Increase competition so more companies want to insure Florida families.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Protect homeowners from abusive claims practices and endless runaround.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Keep Citizens as a backstop, not a growing substitute for a working market.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Tell families the truth about flood risk and storm exposure instead of hiding costs until renewal day.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Measure reform the only way that matters: are premiums coming down, and do claims get paid?

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Your home should not be a luxury item because the insurance system failed. Fix the insurance affordability crisis.

passages.heading: Stop Taxing People Out of Their Homes
passages.text: You worked a lifetime to own your house. Then the county sends another bill for the privilege of living in it. If the value on paper goes up, the tax can go up even when your paycheck does not.

passages.heading: Stop Taxing People Out of Their Homes
passages.text: That hits retirees on fixed incomes first. It hits widows who want to stay on the same street. It hits young families who finally bought a starter home and then learned the tax bill is another mortgage.

passages.heading: Stop Taxing People Out of Their Homes
passages.text: Parents should not have to choose between keeping the house and paying for groceries. Small shops tied to a building feel the same squeeze. Local government got used to spending the increase. Families got used to being told there is no other way.

passages.heading: Stop Taxing People Out of Their Homes
passages.text: There is another way. If you own your home, you should not keep paying rent to the government forever.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Eliminate 100% of property taxes on homesteaded homes . Your home, your money, and your freedom belong to you, not them.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Florida families should never be taxed out of houses they already paid for . Government should live within its means, just like those families do.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Property tax relief is not a gift . It is the state admitting it does not own your house.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Fight to eliminate homestead property taxes so owners are not billed every year for staying in their own home.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Force state and local governments to set priorities and cut waste instead of leaning on the next assessment increase.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Protect retirees and fixed income owners who did everything right and still fear the tax notice.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Be honest that government will have to spend less. That is the point. Families already do.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: If you own your home, you shouldn’t have to keep paying the government for the privilege of living in it.

passages.heading: Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive
passages.text: A young couple wants a starter home near work. The listing is gone in a weekend, or the payment is impossible once insurance and taxes land on top of the mortgage . A teacher rents farther from school each year. A restaurant crew drives an hour because nothing nearby is open at their wage.

passages.heading: Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive
passages.text: That is not only a market story. Rules, delays, and layered approvals make it slower and more expensive to build the homes working people need. When government makes building hard, families pay rent for the delay.

passages.heading: Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive
passages.text: Longtime residents get pushed out of the neighborhoods they helped build . Adult children cannot move back near their parents. Small landlords sell because insurance and taxes ate the margin. “Affordable housing” becomes a slogan while the starter home disappears.

passages.heading: Florida Housing Should Not Be So Expensive
passages.text: Floridians should not have to leave Florida to afford Florida.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Housing gets cheaper when people are free to build, buy, and rent without a maze of permission . Get government out of the way of new homes, especially starter homes.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Property rights matter . So does the ability of working people to live near the jobs that keep this state running.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: We will not pretend a new office in Tallahassee can wish prices down . Cut the barriers.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Strip the red tape that makes ordinary homes take years and extra dollars to approve.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Support local decisions that add starter homes and rentals without turning every project into a political fight.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Stop stacking insurance, tax, and fee costs onto the monthly payment until working families are priced out.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Respect property rights while rejecting the idea that government should pick winners among developers.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Measure success by whether nurses, teachers, tradespeople, and young families can still live in their communities.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Florida should be a place you can start a life, not a place you get priced out of.

passages.heading: Secure Borders. Legal Opportunity.
passages.text: A free country should welcome peaceful people who come here to work, build a life, and join a community . Freedom also depends on knowing who is coming in.

passages.heading: Secure Borders. Legal Opportunity.
passages.text: When the system is slow, confusing, and unfair, honest people wait in line while criminals, traffickers, and cartels look for gaps . That is not compassion. That is a broken process that hurts citizens, legal immigrants, workers, and business owners.

passages.heading: Secure Borders. Legal Opportunity.
passages.text: Florida families feel it in crowded services, strained schools, and job sites where the rules seem to apply to some people and not others . Small business owners who follow the law watch competitors who do not. Communities want order, not chaos and not cruelty.

passages.heading: Secure Borders. Legal Opportunity.
passages.text: The two major parties use this issue to raise money and pick a fight . Floridians want a system that is lawful, faster for honest people, and tough on people who hurt others.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Secure the border. Make legal immigration simpler and faster . Focus enforcement on criminals, traffickers, and real security threats.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Peaceful people who want to work and follow the law should not face a wall of bureaucracy . People who commit crimes should not get a pass.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: The goal is more freedom, less bureaucracy , and a system that is fair to citizens, immigrants, workers, and businesses alike.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Support secure borders and clear enforcement against criminals, traffickers, and genuine security threats.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Push for a simpler, faster legal path so honest people can come, work, and contribute without disappearing into a backlog.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Stop using Floridians as props in a national shouting match.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Protect the rule of law so legal residents and citizens are not asked to ignore the rules everyone else is told to follow.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Judge policy by whether communities are safer and whether peaceful workers have a lawful way in.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Welcome people who come to build a life and assimilate. Stop people who come to harm our way of life. Make the lawful path the easier path.

passages.heading: Parents Should Decide
passages.text: Parents know their children better than any official in Tallahassee. They know how their kid learns. They know when a school is working and when it is not.

passages.heading: Parents Should Decide
passages.text: Too often the system protects itself first . Families get assigned a building and told to be grateful. Teachers get buried in paperwork. Kids who need something different wait. A mom who wants to homeschool, pick a charter, or try a small private school should not have to fight the state for permission to do what is best for her child.

passages.heading: Parents Should Decide
passages.text: Young people starting out need skills that lead to work , not a pile of debt and a diploma that does not open a door. Higher education should serve students, not a bureaucracy.

passages.heading: Parents Should Decide
passages.text: Education is not a turf war between politicians . It is a parent standing in a doorway asking, “Will this help my kid?”

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Parents decide. Funding should follow the student , whether that is a traditional public school, a charter, a private school, homeschool, or another option that fits the child.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: ZIP code and income should not trap a family in a school that is failing their kid . Choice is for every parent, not only the ones who can already buy their way out.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Education should help children succeed. It should not exist to protect a government system.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Put parents in the driver’s seat and keep them there.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Make money follow the child so families have real options, not just a brochure.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Cut the rules that bury teachers in paperwork and pull time away from students.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Keep curriculum decisions close to families. No identity politics in the classroom. Teach kids. Don’t recruit them.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Demand results from schools and colleges that take public money. If it does not help students, it does not get a blank check.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Parents, not bureaucrats, should make the big choices for their kids.

passages.heading: Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use.
passages.text: Healthcare is personal. It is the nurse on a long shift who still cannot afford her own bill. It is the family opening a surprise statement after a short ER visit. It is the worker who loses a job and suddenly wonders if the medicine stays available.

passages.heading: Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use.
passages.text: This year, hundreds of thousands of Floridians lost subsidized coverage or saw prices jump. People did not become less sick. The paperwork and the price tag changed.

passages.heading: Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use.
passages.text: Government keeps adding rules that sound helpful and then show up as higher premiums, narrower networks, and fewer choices . Small business owners trying to cover a crew feel it. Gig workers who buy their own plan feel it. Retirees stuck between systems feel it.

passages.heading: Care You Can Afford. Choices You Can Use.
passages.text: Families do not need another slogan. They need a doctor they can see and a bill they can pay.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Patients and healthcare professionals should come first. People need affordable care and more choices, not a thicker rulebook.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Government should not make healthcare more expensive or more confusing . More options, clearer prices, and fewer barriers beat another layer of control.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: A nurse or doctor should be free to care for patients. A family should be free to pick the coverage that fits their life.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Fight rules that raise premiums and shrink the number of plans families can actually use.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Push for clearer prices so a parent can know the cost before the bill arrives.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Expand choices for workers, small shops, and people who buy coverage on their own.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Keep the focus on patients and the people who treat them, not on protecting a system.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Tell the truth when federal subsidy changes hit Florida households, and refuse to pretend Tallahassee can hide the cost.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: People need care they can reach and a price they can live with. Government should stop making that harder.

passages.heading: Grow Without Crushing Communities
passages.text: Florida is growing because people want to be here. That should be good news. Too often it feels like a traffic jam, a crowded classroom, and a construction fence where a familiar view used to be.

passages.heading: Grow Without Crushing Communities
passages.text: Parents spend half the afternoon in the car. Truck drivers lose hours on the same stretch of road. Homeowners watch a wetland or a tree line vanish and then get told the pipes and schools will “catch up later.” Later usually means another fee.

passages.heading: Grow Without Crushing Communities
passages.text: Growth without capacity is how you get angry neighborhoods and brittle systems . Growth with a pile of special deals is how you get the feeling that someone else got the break.

passages.heading: Grow Without Crushing Communities
passages.text: People are not against the next family moving in. They are against a government that approves the rooftops and forgets the roads, water, and schools those rooftops need.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Communities should grow without being crushed . Infrastructure is not a favor. If you allow the houses, you have to be honest about the roads, water, sewer, and classrooms.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Local people and property owners should have a real voice . Distant agencies and sweetheart incentives should not run the map.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Florida can welcome people and still protect the places that make this state worth living in.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Demand that roads, water, sewer, and schools keep up with growth instead of trailing it by a decade.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Cut the delays that raise costs, then dump those costs on the next buyer.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Stop using taxpayer incentives to force growth the community cannot support.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Respect property rights and local voices when a project changes a neighborhood.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Be honest about tradeoffs. Growth is not free. Neither is pretending the pipes will appear on their own.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Florida can grow and still feel like home. The roads, water, and schools have to keep up, and the special deals have to stop.

passages.heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
passages.text: A family that just finished boarding the windows should not also be praying the insurance company picks up the phone . A fisherman knows the water. A farmer knows the land. A homeowner on a canal knows what happens when the surge comes.

passages.heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
passages.text: Florida lives with storms. That will not change. What can change is whether we keep building the next neighborhood in the next vulnerable place, then acting surprised when the bill arrives. Water quality, the Everglades, and coastal flooding are not abstract “environment” talk. They are drinking water, jobs, and whether the house is still standing.

passages.heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
passages.text: FAU polling found most Floridians worry about stronger storms and worse surge. They are right to. Risk is real. Hiding it until premium day is how families get trapped.

passages.heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
passages.text: Good stewards already live here . They do not need a lecture from a distant agency.

passages.heading: Protect Homes, Water, and Coast
passages.text: They need honest rules, working mitigation , and a government that does not make recovery harder than the storm.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Farmers, fishermen, and homeowners care for the land they live on . Good stewards, not distant agencies, should make the big decisions about their own property.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Protecting water and coast is how you protect homes, jobs, and the next generation’s Florida . Property rights and clean water are not opposites.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Storm readiness and insurance costs are the same conversation . Pretending otherwise is how premiums explode after the season ends.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Support preparedness and mitigation that actually protect homes and businesses, not just press releases after landfall.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Be honest about flood and surge risk so families are not sold a house the system cannot insure.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Protect water quality and the Everglades without burying working people in paperwork that does not clean a single gallon.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Respect property rights. Stop treating every owner like the problem.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Connect storm policy to insurance reform so recovery does not become a second disaster.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Protect the home. Protect the water. Trust the people who live on the land to be good stewards of it.

passages.heading: Government Should Live on a Budget
passages.text: When a family earns less, they cut what they cannot afford . When a small shop has a bad month, the owner skips a draw and watches every receipt. Government does the opposite. It asks for more.

passages.heading: Government Should Live on a Budget
passages.text: Floridians see waste and then get told the answer is another tax, another fee, another program . Retirees who saved carefully watch Tallahassee spend like the well never runs dry. Parents who pack lunches watch agencies grow.

passages.heading: Government Should Live on a Budget
passages.text: Rules pile up. So do hidden costs. A new form does not look like a tax . It still takes a Saturday the shop owner does not have. A camera network does not look like a tax. It still treats free people like suspects for driving to work.

passages.heading: Government Should Live on a Budget
passages.text: Accountability is not a slogan. It is whether anyone can follow the money and say no.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: It is your money . Government should spend it only when the expense is truly necessary.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Lower taxes and tighter budgets force government to set priorities, cut waste, and become accountable. That is how families already live.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Transparency is not optional . Free people have a right to see how they are being governed — and a right not to be tracked just for using the road.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Demand that government live on a budget the way families and small shops already do.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Cut waste before asking taxpayers for another dollar.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Shrink the rulebook that costs time and money without making life safer or better.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Open the books. If the public cannot see it, it should not be spent.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Oppose warrantless tracking of everyday Floridians, including ALPR and Flock style camera networks that log parents, nurses, and delivery drivers.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Stop asking taxpayers for more. Start making government do more with what it already has.

passages.heading: Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights.
passages.text: A store owner should not dread the next smash and grab . A parent should not change the walk to school. A senior living alone should not feel like the easy target. Nurses leaving a night shift should get to the car in peace. "Teen Take Overs" are not an acceptable trend.

passages.heading: Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights.
passages.text: Florida communities need to be safe . That means going after people who hurt others: violent offenders, traffickers, dealers who poison neighborhoods, and crews that treat theft like a business.

passages.heading: Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights.
passages.text: It also means the justice system should spend its time on real threats, not on turning everyday life into a dragnet . Warrantless cameras that log every errand do not make a family safer. They treat free people like suspects.

passages.heading: Keep Communities Safe. Protect Your Rights.
passages.text: Law abiding parents and homeowners have the right to protect their families . Public safety and constitutional rights are not a trade. A free state can do both.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Keep communities safe . Give law enforcement the tools to go after violent crime, trafficking, drugs, and organized theft.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Demand accountability . Focus the justice system on people who pose a real threat. Protect the rights of everyone else.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Free people should not have their every move recorded for driving down the road . This campaign opposes ALPR camera networks and mass surveillance of lawful residents.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Law abiding Floridians have the right to keep and bear arms to protect their homes and families . That right should not be chipped away by politicians who do not trust the people.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Support effective policing aimed at violent crime, trafficking, drugs, and organized theft.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Push courts and prosecutors to focus resources on people who threaten public safety.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Protect constitutional rights, including due process and the right of law abiding people to defend themselves.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Reject mass surveillance of everyday travel, including Flock style ALPR systems.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Give local law enforcement flexibility to solve problems in their own communities, and hold them accountable when they abuse that power.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Safe streets. Free people. Go after real threats. Leave law abiding Floridians alone.

passages.heading: Get Government Out of the Way of Work
passages.text: Nicole and her husband have made payroll since 2007. They know what a new rule from Tallahassee does to a small carpentry shop . It does not hit the politician first. It hits the owner who cannot pass the cost on and the crew that needs hours next week.

passages.heading: Get Government Out of the Way of Work
passages.text: Gig workers picking up weekend rides, parents running a side hustle from the kitchen table, and young people trying to start something all run into the same wall : permits, licenses, and delays that have nothing to do with serving a customer.

passages.heading: Get Government Out of the Way of Work
passages.text: Florida can attract new industries . It can also scare them off with taxes, power bill surprises, and a rulebook that only the big players can afford to read. Workers do not need a slogan about jobs. They need an employer who can afford to hire them.

passages.heading: Get Government Out of the Way of Work
passages.text: A robust economy with more living wage work is how families stay . Government does not create that by adding another office. It creates that by getting out of the way.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Trust people who build things . Small shops, the self employed, and gig workers should be free to earn a living without asking permission for every step.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Keep taxes competitive. Cut rules that make it expensive to hire. Welcome new industries without handing them a taxpayer subsidy.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Scott has built companies and solved hard problems in the private sector . Nicole has kept a family business alive through good years and bad ones. That is the economy they will fight for.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Cut occupational licenses and rules that block people from working.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Make it cheaper and simpler to hire, especially for small shops. Keep Florida competitive on taxes without selling the state off through special deals.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Support workforce paths that lead to real jobs, trades, skills, and new industries, instead of paperwork theaters.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Say no to barriers that protect connected companies and punish the next startup.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Let Floridians work, hire, and build. The best jobs plan is less permission and more freedom.

passages.heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
passages.text: A potential simple solution: The data center provides its own power, uses an internal heat exchange cooling system similar to a car radiator, and is not built near neighborhoods or cities. This way they don't use existing power grids or existing water supplies.

passages.heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
passages.text: A retiree on a fixed income should not see the power bill jump because a warehouse of computers moved in down the road. A small shop should not subsidize the water and substations of a company that could write a check.

passages.heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
passages.text: Artificial intelligence is bringing real investment. That can mean jobs and better tools. It can also mean massive data centers that gulp electricity, water, and land.

passages.heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
passages.text: When government hands out incentives and then quietly socializes the infrastructure, ordinary Floridians pick up the tab .

passages.heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
passages.text: Neighbors worry about wells, wetlands , and whether the next rate case will treat a tech campus like just another customer. Property owners worry about eminent domain dressed up as “economic development.” Parents wonder why their light bill is part of someone else’s business plan.

passages.heading: Don’t Make Families Pay Big Tech’s Bill
passages.text: Florida should not be for sale. Innovation is welcome. A hidden tax on households is not.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Welcome technological investment . Do not force residents and small businesses to subsidize it.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Data centers should pay their own way for power, water, land, and grid upgrades . Taxpayers should not underwrite some of the world’s largest technology companies.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Energy policy should serve Florida families first . That includes cleaner, safer, reliable power, and it includes nuclear as part of a serious energy future.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Property rights and local voices come before ribbon cuttings.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Require data centers and similar projects to cover the power, water, and infrastructure they use instead of shifting costs onto household rates.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: End taxpayer incentives that socialize the downside and privatize the upside for giant tech firms.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Protect property rights and water resources when a project changes a community.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Plan energy capacity for Florida homes and shops first, then for industrial demand that pays its own bill.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Support cleaner, safer, reliable energy, including nuclear, so the state is not stuck choosing between growth and brownouts.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Florida should welcome builders and innovators. It should not put their power bill on your kitchen table.

passages.heading: Your Drive Home Is Not a Government File
passages.text: Flock cameras do not just look for criminals . They quietly track everyday Floridians. A parent driving kids to school. A nurse heading to a night shift. A small business owner making deliveries. A retiree going to the store. The camera does not care why you were on that road. It logs you anyway.

passages.heading: Your Drive Home Is Not a Government File
passages.text: Once that data is collected, it can be searched and shared . Often without a warrant. Often without you ever knowing. A system built to catch a stolen car becomes a system that can reconstruct your week.

passages.heading: Your Drive Home Is Not a Government File
passages.text: That is not how free people should live. You should be able to drive home without becoming a line in a government file. Safety does not require treating every law abiding driver like a suspect.

passages.heading: Your Drive Home Is Not a Government File
passages.text: Communities still need real policing aimed at real threats. Tracking every errand is not the same thing. It is cheaper for government to watch everyone than to do the harder work of going after people who actually hurt others.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Free people should not have their every move recorded by the government just for driving down the road.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: This campaign is against Flock cameras. It is against ALPR networks. It is against warrantless mass tracking of lawful residents.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: If police have a suspect and a warrant, they can do their job. That is a far cry from logging parents, nurses, and delivery drivers by default.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Your life is your business. Getting to work is not probable cause.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Oppose Flock cameras and all ALPR systems that scan and store the movements of everyday Floridians.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Fight the spread of these networks in cities, counties, and along Florida roads.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Demand a warrant before government searches travel data that can rebuild a person’s day.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Stop selling “public safety” as a reason to watch people who have done nothing wrong.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Keep law enforcement focused on violent crime, trafficking, and real threats, not on building a map of every drive to school and every night shift.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: You should be able to drive your kids to school without the government keeping the receipt. We are against Flock cameras. Period.

passages.heading: Parents Have the Right to Protect Their Families
passages.text: A law abiding parent should not have to ask permission to protect their kids . A homeowner should not have to hope the sheriff arrives in time. A woman closing a shop at night should not be told her right to defend herself is a talking point for later.

passages.heading: Parents Have the Right to Protect Their Families
passages.text: Politicians who do not trust the people keep chipping away at that right . Another rule. Another list. Another delay. None of it stops a criminal who already ignores the law. It does land on the nurse, the truck driver, and the retiree who followed every rule and still gets treated like the problem.

passages.heading: Parents Have the Right to Protect Their Families
passages.text: Florida families live in the real world. They lock the doors . They walk a dark parking lot. They want their children safe. The Second Amendment was written for those people, not for a committee in Tallahassee.

passages.heading: Parents Have the Right to Protect Their Families
passages.text: Scott and Nicole trust you with your own life . That includes the tools you use to protect it.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Law abiding parents and homeowners have the right to protect their families . That right should not be chipped away by politicians who do not trust the people.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: This campaign is pro Second Amendment. No half measures . Support the right to possess, carry, and modify weapons and accessories for self defense and to keep a free people free.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: We support open carry and constitutional carry in Florida . We oppose restrictions on weapons, ammunition, and accessories, unless a private property owner sets those rules on their own premises.

passages.heading: What Scott and Nicole Believe
passages.text: Private property still belongs to the owner. Your rights do not stop at the state line, and they do not disappear because someone in office got nervous.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Defend the right of law abiding Floridians to keep and bear arms without a new stack of permission slips.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Support constitutional carry and open carry in Florida. Oppose new restrictions on weapons, ammunition, and accessories.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Respect the right of private property owners to set rules on their own premises, and stop government from setting those rules for everyone else.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Reject the idea that trusting free people is dangerous, and that trusting politicians with a monopoly on force is safe.

passages.heading: What We Will Do
passages.text: Keep the focus on criminals who use guns to hurt people, not on parents and homeowners who keep one to stay alive.

passages.heading: Official Mission Statement
passages.text: Our mission is to keep Florida the best state in America by trusting people more than government. We will shrink overreach, stop wasting your tax dollars, defend your rights, and get Tallahassee out of the way, so you can keep what you earn, raise your kids as you see fit, and live free.

passages.heading: Official Mission Statement
passages.text: Floridians are working harder than ever . Government keeps making life more expensive and more complicated. We’re running as Libertarians because we trust you. Keep more of what you earn. Raise your kids your way. Live without a stack of new rules from Tallahassee or Washington. If you want leaders who get out of the way instead of standing in it, stand with us.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: They match what the Libertarian Party of Florida stands for, said the way this campaign talks, people first, in plain words.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: You own your life . You are free to live it your way, as long as you don’t hurt anyone else.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: Government should stay small. It should only do the things people truly cannot do for themselves.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: Hardworking Floridians should keep more of what they earn . Government should live on a budget, take only what is truly needed, and stop treating taxpayers like an open wallet.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: Your home, your property , and the results of your work belong to you, not to politicians.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: Parental choice . Parents, not bureaucrats, decide what’s best for their kids.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: People should speak, worship, associate, and defend themselves without asking permission.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: Second amendment. Law abiding parents and homeowners have the right to protect their families.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: Your private life is not the government’s business . Free people should not be tracked for driving down the road.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: Let people and businesses compete fairly . Government should not pick winners and losers.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: No one is above the law, not an individual, not a corporation, and not government. End the waste, the fraud, and the special deals.

passages.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
passages.text: If you already live this way, work hard, take care of your family, and want to be left alone, you are not extreme. You are the Florida we are running to serve.

passages.heading: A mission is a promise you can measure. Here is ours.
passages.text: Stop the squeeze on families . Cut the rules and costs that hit parents, gig workers, tradespeople, nurses, teachers, and small shops first.

passages.heading: A mission is a promise you can measure. Here is ours.
passages.text: Fix the insurance affordability crisis . Homeowners should not pay some of the highest premiums in the country for coverage that fails them when a storm hits.

passages.heading: A mission is a promise you can measure. Here is ours.
passages.text: Stop taxing people out of their homes. If you own your homestead, you should not keep paying the government for the privilege of living in it.

passages.heading: A mission is a promise you can measure. Here is ours.
passages.text: Put parents in the driver’s seat. Education money should follow the child. Parents know their kids better than Tallahassee does.

passages.heading: A mission is a promise you can measure. Here is ours.
passages.text: Secure the border and open a lawful path to work. Welcome peaceful people who come to build a life. Focus enforcement on criminals, traffickers, and real threats.

passages.heading: A mission is a promise you can measure. Here is ours.
passages.text: Protect your rights and your privacy. Defend the Constitution, the Second Amendment, and the Fourth. Your drive home is not a government file.

passages.heading: A mission is a promise you can measure. Here is ours.
passages.text: Make government live on a budget. Families do it. Small businesses do it. Tallahassee should have to do it too.

passages.heading: Why Libertarian
passages.text: The Libertarian Party of Florida says you own your life. We agree. We will uphold and defend the Constitution, not just talk about it during campaign season. This campaign is for every Floridian. The smallest minority is the individual. That is who we serve.

passages.heading: Libertarian Candidate for Governor of Florida, 2026
passages.text: Scott Jewett is a businessman, innovator, and lifelong problem solver who calls Boca Raton home. Like millions of Floridians, he and his wife Regina live with the daily realities of rising insurance costs, property taxes, and the stubborn question of how to leave a freer, more prosperous Florida for the next generation.

passages.heading: Libertarian Candidate for Governor of Florida, 2026
passages.text: He's running for Florida Governor because he believes Florida can do better , with less government overreach, more individual liberty, and practical solutions that put people first.

passages.heading: A Family Man Who Calls Florida Home
passages.text: Scott and Regina live in Boca Raton, where they face the same insurance premiums, property costs, and everyday pressures that millions of their neighbors know all too well. For Scott, this isn't abstract policy; it's personal. He has drafted concrete proposals to reform Florida's broken homeowners insurance system because he's lived the frustration of paying far more in premiums than is ever paid back in claims. He is the only candidate who has attended the legislative sessions in person, and he's fighting to eliminate property tax for every homestead homeowner in the state.

passages.heading: A Family Man Who Calls Florida Home
passages.text: Family is central to how Scott sees the world: protect what matters, take responsibility, and leave things better than you found them . After marrying Regina in 2019, he welcomed her two sons, Jamie and Jonathon, into his life, and he is father to two daughters, Alexandra and Savannah. "I am proud to carry forward a legacy of Libertarian values passed down from my father and grandfather. Raised with a commitment to helping those in need and upholding strong ethical standards, these principles have guided me throughout my life."

passages.heading: From the Garage to the Global Stage
passages.text: Born in Seattle in 1959 and raised in San Diego, Scott was the kind of kid who preferred the canyons and the garage to sitting still in a classroom . His father, Harvey, an aerospace engineer, would bring home real engineering problems for his son to tinker with. By age 11, Scott was building and selling custom furniture and dollhouses. At 16 he took a job as a dishwasher at a Bonanza Steakhouse; by 18 he was in management. The carpet cleaning business he launched with a partner in those early years is still operating today.

passages.heading: From the Garage to the Global Stage
passages.text: He went on to earn both his bachelor's degree and his MBA in business management from San Diego State University, a combination of hands on grit and formal training that shaped everything that followed.

passages.heading: Entrepreneur, Inventor, and Builder
passages.text: Scott is the kind of person who sees a problem and starts sketching a solution. He holds more than a dozen U.S. and international patents spanning oil and gas safety, force mitigation systems, construction, medical devices, and energy. His work includes:

passages.heading: Entrepreneur, Inventor, and Builder
passages.text: Blast mitigation systems that still protect the walls of the Pentagon after 9/11, along with similar protections for other high profile buildings.

passages.heading: Entrepreneur, Inventor, and Builder
passages.text: Oil well integrity solutions developed with BP and Shell to help prevent disasters like the Deepwater Horizon blowout.

passages.heading: Entrepreneur, Inventor, and Builder
passages.text: Advanced ballistic composites that outperformed traditional armor materials in military applications.

passages.heading: Entrepreneur, Inventor, and Builder
passages.text: Wisp Energy, which he founded to develop more efficient wind and wave turbines, work accepted into Florida Atlantic University's Tech Runway incubator, supported by a National Science Foundation grant pathway and a research partnership with the University of California, Irvine.

passages.heading: Entrepreneur, Inventor, and Builder
passages.text: As a business builder, Scott grew LINE X from a young franchise system into more than 600 locations across 23 countries , with system wide sales exceeding $160 million and repeated appearances on Entrepreneur Magazine's fastest growing franchises list before leading the company's sale. In 2018, he and his family acquired Pinspiration, a creative DIY studio concept, and grew it into a national franchise with dozens of locations.

passages.heading: Entrepreneur, Inventor, and Builder
passages.text: Along the way, he has advised more than 250 companies, including 20th Century Fox, Tyco, West Marine, Denny's, and Drybar , helping them scale, franchise, and operate more effectively. He is the author of The Ultimate Guide to Becoming a Franchisee and is at work on a second book on practical economics.

passages.heading: Liberty, Responsibility, and Looking Out for One Another
passages.text: Scott describes his philosophy as Humanitarian Libertarianism : free people looking out for each other. He believes the proper role of government is to protect individual rights, keep people safe, and then get out of the way so that families, entrepreneurs, and communities can thrive.

passages.heading: Liberty, Responsibility, and Looking Out for One Another
passages.text: He is a strong supporter of the Second Amendment and responsible gun ownership . He has long backed organizations that help people in need — including Big Brothers Big Sisters, the Make A Wish Foundation, Goodwill, and World Vision — served on the board of a recovery organization, and quietly helped individuals rebuild their lives.

passages.heading: Liberty, Responsibility, and Looking Out for One Another
passages.text: " As a Libertarian, my focus is on empowering individuals , reducing government intervention, and promoting freedom and personal responsibility. Together, we can make Florida a place where freedom thrives and people are empowered to live their best lives."

passages.heading: Why Scott Is Running for Governor for FLorida
passages.text: Florida faces real pressures: insurance costs that push fixed income residents out of their homes, housing that's out of reach for too many working families, an education system that too often fails to prepare kids for the future, and a government that keeps testing the limits of personal freedom.

passages.heading: Why Scott Is Running for Governor for FLorida
passages.text: Scott is not a career politician. He's a builder who has solved hard problems in the private sector and for the Department of Defense . He has already drafted insurance reform legislation and a detailed plan, because he refuses to accept that Floridians should keep paying six times more in premiums than they ever receive back in claims.

passages.heading: Why Scott Is Running for Governor for FLorida
passages.text: His agenda centers on a strong economy with more living wage jobs , real educational choice, public safety, lower taxes, and a government that respects the rights of every Floridian, regardless of which party they usually vote for.

passages.heading: Why Scott Is Running for Governor for FLorida
passages.text: This is our moment to choose a different path: one that trusts free people to look out for each other and build the Florida we all want to live in.

passage.text: Floridians are feeling the squeeze every month . Insurance premiums keep climbing, everyday costs keep rising, and too much of your hard earned money disappears into government waste. Scott Jewett is fighting to fix the insurance affordability crisis, cut taxes, shrink the size of government, and put real solutions in place that help families keep more of what they earn. He believes Florida can do better when we put people first .

passage.text: Government rules and state programs keep pushing your insurance higher. We will cut those rules and open the market so more companies compete for your business. More competition means lower premiums for Florida homeowners.

passage.text: Eliminate 100% of property taxes on homesteaded homes . Your home, your money, and your freedom belong to you, not them.

passage.text: Keep communities safe . Give law enforcement the tools to go after violent crime, trafficking, drugs, and organized theft.

passage.text: Push courts and prosecutors to focus resources on people who threaten public safety.

passage.text: Stop selling “public safety” as a reason to watch people who have done nothing wrong.

passage.heading: What We Will Do
passage.text: Oppose warrantless tracking of everyday Floridians, including ALPR and Flock style camera networks that log parents, nurses, and delivery drivers.

passage.heading: What We Will Do

passage.heading: These are not talking points. They are the line we will not cross.
